paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. God gave Ephraim and Manasseh their land, and the borders were drawn, but living in it took work. They did not drive out the Canaanites in Gezer (Joshua 16:10), and Manasseh was unable to occupy those cities (Joshua 17:12). When they grew stronger, they still "failed to drive them out completely" (Joshua 17:13). Getting a gift and walking all the way into it are two different things, and I know a thing or two about a gift that needs unpacking.

Then the sons of Joseph came to Joshua with a complaint. They said they had many people and the hill country wasn't enough, and they pointed at the iron chariots (Joshua 17:14-16). I think they were looking at the size of the problem and not at the size of what they'd been given. Joshua told them, "You have many people and great strength," and then, "Although the Canaanites have iron chariots and although they are strong, you can drive them out" (Joshua 17:17-18). Friend, he pointed to what they already had and told them to get to work.

Notice the daughters of Zelophehad too. They went to Eleazar the priest, Joshua and the leaders and said, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers," and Joshua gave it to them, "in keeping with the command of the LORD" (Joshua 17:4). They held on to what God had said, and they asked. So when God has spoken, don't shrink from it and don't make excuses. Hold onto His word, take the next step, and clear your forest.
